First, we find ${f}^{′}(t)$ by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+2)^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\frac{t}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}},\,2(t+2)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute ${f}^{′}(\pi )$ we substitute $t=\pi $ into the expression for ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi ,\,\frac{\pi }{\sqrt{{\pi }^{2}+1}},\,2(\pi +2)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,\frac{\pi }{\sqrt{{\pi }^{2}+1}},\,2(\pi +2)⟩\end{aligned}
$$
